Consult Summary:
- One-line: Acute wheeze with history of childhood asthma and seasonal hay fever; plan for objective testing (pulse oximetry) to differentiate asthma vs dust allergy, plus PCP follow-up and possible steroids based on results.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing starting ~2 days ago after dust exposure while cleaning; nocturnal worsening; progressing shortness of breath and difficulty speaking at times.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began about 2 days ago; gradually worse, especially at night.
- Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath when talking; sometimes unable to complete sentences; no chest pain; no dizziness.
- Past medical history: Childhood asthma (mostly resolved); summer hay fever; uses an asthma inhaler; not regularly seen a doctor for asthma; inhaler possibly from a few months ago.
- Allergies: None known.
- Medications: Inhaler used in the past/potentially current; antihistamines not at home; antihistamine discussion for potential allergy management; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Proximity to primary care clinic (minutes away); no smoking information provided.
- Preventive care: Not specified.

Examination:
- (No physical examination or vitals documented.)

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Possible asthma exacerbation or dust-triggered allergic reaction; need objective testing to differentiate asthma vs allergy.

Plan:
- Tests and investigations:
  - Urgent in-person clinic visit for objective testing.
  - Pulse oximetry (finger probe) to assess oxygen saturation.
- Treatments/medication considerations:
  - If allergy suspected, consider antihistamine; OTC use discussed; dose/route/frequency not documented; PCP can prescribe if not available.
  - Potential need for steroids now if indicated after testing (decision deferred until results).
- Follow-up/communication:
  - Letter to PCP to inform of the visit; app-based delivery of the letter; PCP appointment estimated to take about 10 minutes.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals and any physical examination findings; full medication reconciliation (inhaler type, current use, dose, route, frequency); explicit allergy details beyond “none known”; smoking status.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in transcript.
- Transcript quality: Brief video signal disruption occurred; otherwise content sufficient to form plan.
